editorial: Editorial, reviewed in data PRs: the broad groups the estimate's depth themes read (specs/chances/method/standing.md "Revision 3"). Owner, 2026-10-12: "Business has ties in with math, statistics, computer science. We should more loosely have concepts of STEM vs arts… a good way to loosely group will make it easier to draw a depth conclusion; that's how a student's essays and recommendations tie things together, and we don't have those." Three course groups, modeled on the meta-majors colleges use to sort programs (STEM; social and behavioral sciences with the humanities; arts), with business split across STEM and the social sciences the way the federal STEM list (econometrics, quantitative and cognitive psychology) and the NSF's science-and-engineering fields (psychology, economics) cross the College Board's own AP categories. Athletics, service, and faith sit outside every course group (the Common App lists them as their own activity types), so they never make a theme and never count as connected to a major. A course reads by its subject family unless `courses` names it; an activity reads by its family (lib/chances/types.ts ActivityFamily).
